title: Heterogeneous GPU-type headroom mismatch causing silent burst denials
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Observed repeated customer escalations where tenants experienced silent burst denials during multi-instance-type reserved-pool bursts. The autoscaler reported apparent spare headroom, but requests were denied when routed to mixed-GPU pools. This ticket tracks diagnosis, emergency patch, canary rollout, and postmortem actions.
comments: 2026-03-10: Incident reported by Support after ACMEHealth reported sudden burst denials during morning traffic spike. Pager escalated to Capacity SRE and Autoscaler team.

2026-03-10: Initial triage: metrics show reserved_pool_headroom>0 but tenant_request_admissions logged 'denied:flavor-mismatch' in allocator. Hypothesis: headroom accounting normalized incorrectly across GPU flavors.
2026-03-11: Reproduced locally by simulating mixed-GPU reserved pool (A100 + V100) and tenant burst. Observed allocation decisions using 'logical_slots' without weighting by per-flavor capacity unit.
2026-03-11: Added temporary telemetry: reserved_headroom_by_flavor, tenant_burst_denials_by_flavor. Dashboard created and shared with Eng/PM/Support.

2026-03-12: Drafted fix to allocator normalization (PR #4921). Patch changes: compute capacity_units = gpu_type_capacity[gpu_flavor] and use flavor-weighted slot assignment; add per-tenant flavor-aware reservations.
2026-03-12: Hotfix staged to canary cluster in us-west1; initial rollout 5% traffic. Monitoring shows denied_count_by_flavor fall 90% for canary tenants.
2026-03-13: Expanded rollout to 25% after smoke tests passed. Support notified customers and applied temporary burst-credit refunds to affected tenants.
2026-03-14: Observed reduction in customer escalations; still monitoring edge cases where KV-cache eviction + preemption causes transient denials. Next: full rollout and regression tests.
next_steps: Merge PR #4921 and promote to production after 48h canary validation
Add unit/regression tests for mixed-flavor headroom accounting
Update runbook: add flavor-aware check during reserved pool audits
Create long-term design: normalize capacity units across cloud providers and add autoscaler validation job
Schedule customer follow-up comms for impacted accounts and billing reconciliations
summary: Root cause: autoscaler's headroom accounting treated GPU slots as uniform units. In mixed-flavor pools (different compute / memory per GPU), the allocator counted slots instead of weighted capacity units which led to overcommitting logical slots and silent denials when requests were assigned to lower-capacity flavors. Hotfix: flavor-weighted capacity normalization and per-tenant flavor reservations; canary rollout in progress.
